inputs.model: Look-through earnings capitalization (proportionate EBITDAF) cross-checked against, and finally blended with, portfolio NAV/sum-of-parts
inputs.model_rationale: Infratil is an externally managed infrastructure investment HOLDCO, not an operating company. The dcf-methods routing table puts a holdco between two rows: 'Insurer, holdco, compounder-of-book -> BVPS compounding x exit P/B' and 'LIC / investment trust -> NAV + exit discount'. The skill's instruction for a straddle is to value the parts and say so. Infratil straddles because it is neither a passive fund (it controls and operates its investees) nor an operating company (it has no consolidated revenue/margin structure that means anything: NetIncome is portfolio revaluation noise, FY2025 net parent surplus was -NZ$286.3m). So the primary engine is a capitalization of look-through proportionate earnings, and the NAV/SOTP is carried as a co-equal anchor rather than a footnote. The prior model (2026-06-29) used the same framing and it is retained.
inputs.notes: FCF PROXY REBUILT THIS CYCLE - the prior base was wrong in two directions and the correction is the single biggest change in this refresh. Prior model used 989.4 - 124 = 865.4. The FY26 Annual Results Presentation reconciliation (IFT.NZ_Metrics_FY2026.txt lines 1058-1081) prints the actual build: Operational EBITDAF 1,113.7, less Development Spend (70.1), less Corporate costs (124.3) = Proportionate EBITDAF (continuing) 919.3. Arithmetic proof that the headline NZ$989.4m ALREADY has corporate costs deducted and does NOT have development spend deducted: 1,113.7 - 124.3 = 989.4 exactly. The same construction holds for FY25: 1,008.1 - 112.8 = 895.3, matching the presentation's FY25 EBITDAF bar of 895 (and confirmed by the disclosed uplift, 989.4 - 94.1 = 895.3). NOTE ON THE CSV COMPARATIVE: the Metrics CSV stores ShareOfEBITDAF FY2025 = 917.8, which is the 'Total Proportionate EBITDAF' line and INCLUDES the now-discontinued Manawa Energy and RetireAustralia; FY2026 = 989.4 is Operational EBITDAF, which EXCLUDES discontinued operations (FY26 presentation footnote 1: 'includes corporate costs for the purposes of comparison to guidance and excludes discontinued operations'). The two CSV cells are therefore on DIFFERENT bases and a naive FY25->FY26 read gives +7.8% against the company's reported +11%. The like-for-like FY2025 figure is 895.3. The basis break is discontinued operations, not corporate costs. Therefore the prior 989.4 - 124 (a) deducted corporate costs a SECOND time and (b) never deducted the NZ$70.1m of non-capitalised development spend at Gurin/Galileo/Mint, which is real recurring cash out the door. Both errors are fixed by taking the filing's own bottom line, 919.3. Note the two errors partially offset (-124 vs -70.1), which is why the prior 865.4 was only ~6% below the right figure and the error was not obvious in a single valuation. INCENTIVE FEE DEDUCTION: the presentation's own EBITDAF definition (line 37) says EBITDAF 'excludes acquisition and sale-related transaction costs, management incentive fees, and one-off project costs'. Base management fees ARE inside the 124.3 corporate-cost line (Morrison base fee was NZ$101.4m in FY26, Note 28/29), but INCENTIVE fees are excluded from EBITDAF altogether. Those accrue to Morrison, not to shareholders, so an EBITDAF-based valuation overstates the shareholder claim unless they are charged. NZ$35m/yr is deducted as a through-cycle estimate, giving last_fcf 919.3 - 35.0 = 884.3. Sizing: incentive fees are earned only on non-NZ assets for valuation growth above a 12% hurdle (Chair's report, line 325-328); Infratil's own NAV bridge deducts a PV of the management agreement of NZ$1,168.4m covering base + incentive fees discounted over five years, and NZ$35m/yr over five years at 10.5% is ~NZ$131m of PV, i.e. deliberately a fraction of that total because the base-fee portion is already inside corporate costs. This is an estimate, not a disclosed figure, and it is the softest input in the model. NET DEBT restated to 2,987.5 = 3,204.6 at 31-Mar-2026 less NZ$217.1m Fortysouth sale proceeds received 10-Apr-2026 (Note 31 Events After Balance Date). Fortysouth's NZ$15.6m EBITDAF is correspondingly absent from the 919.3 continuing base, so the two are consistent. SBC: NZ$1.2m is immaterial (0.13% of the FCF base, 0.007% of market cap) and is NOT deducted from the flow. For this externally managed holdco the economically meaningful compensation leak is the Morrison management and incentive fee (NZ$101.4m base + incentive), not employee share-based payment - Infratil has almost no direct employees. The field is populated for completeness per the eval, but readers should treat the management fee, not SBC, as the compensation line that matters here.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS and FCF CAGRs are not calculable: net parent surplus is portfolio-revaluation noise (FY2025 -NZ$286.3m, FY2026 +NZ$549.8m). Growth is measured on proportionate EBITDAF and NAV. IMPORTANT BASIS CHANGE HANDLED THIS CYCLE: FY27 guidance of NZ$1,300-1,400m is prepared EXCLUDING corporate costs, whereas the FY26 headline NZ$989.4m INCLUDES them (presentation line 1076-1077). Comparing the two raw would imply 31-42% growth, which is spurious. On the like-for-like ex-corporate basis the company's own figure is ~21%. On this model's continuing basis (after BOTH development spend and corporate costs, the basis on which last_fcf is struck) FY27 guidance implies: low 1,300 - 110 dev - 170 corp = 1,020 (+11.0%); mid 1,350 - 102.5 - 160 = 1,087.5 (+18.3%); high 1,400 - 95 - 150 = 1,155 (+25.6%). The range is far wider on this basis than on the headline basis because corporate costs (124.3 -> 150-170, +21-37%) and development spend (70.1 -> 95-110, +36-57%) are BOTH guided to rise much faster than EBITDAF. Base-case Y1 growth is therefore set at 18%, the guidance midpoint on a consistent basis, NOT the 20% the prior model carried and NOT the 21% headline like-for-like.
historical_growth.notes: FY26 actual growth on the continuing basis was 11.2% (826.7 -> 919.3). The base case assumes that MORE THAN DOUBLES to 18.3% in FY27 purely on guidance. That is the central fragility of this valuation and it is stress-tested in the bear case, which uses 8% - below both the FY26 actual and the bottom of the guidance range - to represent guidance being missed.

base.notes: Y1 18% = FY27 guidance midpoint rebased to the continuing basis (see growth_divergence_warning). Reduced from the prior model's 20%, which was anchored to the headline guidance ratio without adjusting for the corporate-cost basis change. Y2-Y5 taper as the CDC ramp annualises and the development-spend and corporate-cost lines - both growing faster than EBITDAF - continue to absorb a rising share of look-through earnings. WACC 10.5% built in NZD to match NZD flows: NZ 10-yr government bond ~4.5% + beta 1.2 x ERP 5.0% + 0.5% complexity/external-management premium. Terminal 3.0% = long-run NZD nominal GDP. GUIDANCE REAFFIRMED: FY27 guidance of NZ$1,300-1,400m was explicitly reaffirmed unchanged at the 18-August-2026 AGM, five months into the financial year. That is recent, specific corroboration and it is why the base case still anchors Y1 to the guidance midpoint despite FY26 actual growth of only 11.2%.

bull.notes: Y1 26% approximates the TOP of FY27 guidance on the continuing basis (+25.6%), i.e. EBITDAF at NZ$1,400m with corporate costs and development spend at the LOW end of their guided ranges - the combination that maximises look-through earnings. Beyond Y1: CDC sustains the AI-datacentre ramp past the contracted 1GW, Longroad reaches its US$1bn run-rate EBITDAF ambition, Kao Data scales in the UK, and the NAV discount closes. WACC 9.5% reflects the completed debt-platform reset and BBB+ rating maturing.

bear.notes: Y1 8% is deliberately set BELOW the bottom of FY27 guidance on the continuing basis (+11.0%) and below FY26 actual (11.2%), because the bear case is precisely the case where guidance is missed. Drivers: the AI capex cycle cools and CDC's contracted ramp slips; One NZ continues to deteriorate (its portfolio value FELL 8.8% in FY26, from NZ$3,713.5m to NZ$3,386.7m - the only major asset to decline and an underappreciated drag); NZ macro weakness hits Wellington Airport and RHCNZ; corporate costs and development spend keep compounding faster than earnings. WACC 12% prices concentration risk in a single asset (CDC = 43% of portfolio) plus the equity-issuance dependency. POST-JUNE EVIDENCE ADDED: the bear case now also carries CDC mark-to-model risk explicitly. CDC's independent valuation rose 23.6% in the June-2026 quarter to A$18.5bn while its OWN assessed cost of equity ROSE from 11.84% to 12.45% on a higher risk-free rate - i.e. the uplift came entirely from pipeline and contract assumptions (leasable pipeline 2.6GW -> 3.9GW through FY2040), against a headwind from the discount rate, not from cheaper capital. A 43%-of-portfolio unlisted asset re-marked upward 23.6% in one quarter on model inputs is precisely what a bear case should refuse to extrapolate. Additional dated risks now reflected: the OBBBA tightened IRA credit timelines (construction start by 4-Jul-2026, in-service by 31-Dec-2027, plus FEOC rules) which is a concrete threat to Longroad economics, and Longroad's underlying USD valuation has already EASED on higher base rates with the NZD-translated value rising only on FX; the July-2026 NZ government proposal to reallocate Spark/One NZ 2600MHz spectrum to 2degrees compounds One NZ's 8.8% FY26 value decline; and Wellington Airport passengers fell to 5.1m from 5.3m.

entry_price.method: PV of the five interim look-through earnings streams plus the terminal value, both discounted at a 15% hurdle rather than at WACC, less net debt, per share.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth. Base cell (10.5%, 3.0%) = 14.95. The grid spans 10.07 to 26.26, i.e. the answer moves by more than 2.5x across a plausible parameter range. For a holdco whose terminal value is 73% of the base valuation, this width is the honest headline: the NAV anchor at 16.48 is a tighter piece of evidence than any single cell here.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Changed from the prior model's 20/50/30 to 25/50/25. Two reasons, both evidence-driven. (1) The entire base case now rests on FY27 guidance that implies growth of 18.3% against FY26 actual of 11.2% - a doubling that has not yet been demonstrated in a printed result, so the probability of a miss deserves more weight. (2) The bull case was trimmed because the FY26 portfolio table shows the growth is narrower than headline: One NZ, the second-largest holding, DECLINED 8.8% in value, and Galileo and RHCNZ also fell. CDC is carrying the portfolio nearly alone. Offsetting these, the post-balance-date debt refinancing to ~NZ$2.1bn of committed facilities with 1/3/5-year tenors materially reduces the refinancing-stress leg the prior bear case leaned on - which is why bear was not raised above 25%.

checks.detail: Base look-through IV NZ$14.95 vs restated NAV NZ$16.48/share (0.91x). The DCF landing modestly BELOW NAV is the correct and expected relationship here, and is a stronger result than the prior model's near-parity: NAV is struck on independent/market valuations of mostly unlisted assets and does not fully discount for the fact that realising it requires either asset sales or continued capital raising. A look-through earnings capitalization landing above NAV would have been the flag.

Market EV NZ$17,397m (price NZ$14.42 x 999.3m shares + net debt NZ$2,987.5m) on FY26 continuing proportionate EBITDAF of NZ$919.3m = 18.9x. Base-case DCF-implied EV/EBITDAF = 19.5x. The two are within 3%, so the model is not asserting a valuation the market has not already broadly accepted. On FY27 guidance rebased to the continuing basis (NZ$1,087.5m midpoint) the market multiple falls to 16.0x forward.

At NZ$14.42 the stock trades at 0.88x restated NAV of NZ$16.48 (0.89x the as-reported NZ$16.26). Infratil has historically traded in a roughly 0.90x-1.30x P/NAV band, so the current level is at or slightly below the bottom of that range. That is the bull observation. The counter-argument, which the model deliberately does not suppress: NAV is itself struck at a moment when AI-datacentre comparables are elevated, and CDC alone is 43% of portfolio value, so the NAV denominator carries mark-to-model risk that a discount may be rationally pricing rather than mistakenly ignoring.

Probability-weighted IV NZ$15.35 vs current NZ$14.42 = 6.4% upside. This is a materially thinner margin of safety than the prior model reported (14.0% at NZ$15.32), and the reduction is driven by fundamentals, not by the price move: the FCF base was corrected downward for development spend and incentive fees, and Y1 growth was cut from 20% to 18% on the guidance basis change. A 6.4% weighted upside against a 15% hurdle rate means the stock is close to fair, not cheap.

checks.check: Bear case IV vs NAV floor
checks.detail: Bear IV NZ$7.15 is 43% of restated NAV NZ$16.48. This is a known structural artefact of capitalizing a depressed earnings stream at a 12% WACC and is NOT a forecast that the equity is worth NZ$7.15. Infratil's assets are separable and saleable - FY26 alone saw Manawa, RetireAustralia and Fortysouth exited at or near carrying value - so a realistic distressed outcome is a discounted-NAV liquidation at perhaps 0.65-0.80x NAV, i.e. NZ$10.70-13.20, well above the DCF bear output. The bear DCF should be read as 'what the earnings stream alone is worth if growth stalls', with the asset backing as a separate and higher floor. This FLAG is carried forward from the prior model, where it was correctly identified.

Terminal value is 72.9% of base enterprise value (78.7% in bull). High but not anomalous for long-life infrastructure with 30-year CDC contracts and 15-25 year renewable PPAs. Flagged rather than passed because it means the valuation is principally an assertion about the terminal multiple, and the sensitivity grid should be read as the primary output rather than the single base cell.

checks.check: Look-through earnings vs actual cash available to shareholders
checks.detail: THE MOST IMPORTANT CAVEAT IN THIS FILE. Proportionate EBITDAF is NOT free cash flow. FY26 proportionate capex was NZ$2,687m against proportionate EBITDAF of NZ$919.3m, and FY27 capex is guided at NZ$3,800-4,400m (+53%). Infratil is deeply cash-flow negative at the portfolio level and funds the gap with debt and equity issuance (shares 968.1m -> 999.3m in FY26; net debt 2,187.8 -> 3,204.6). The valuation therefore rests on the proposition that this capex compounds into future look-through earnings and portfolio value, NOT on any near-term distributable cash. Nothing in this DCF should be read as implying shareholders can extract NZ$884m a year.

Historical FY-end multiples (Mar-31 FY, March close, on the ShareOfEBITDAF headline basis): EV/EBITDAF 13.01/13.85/13.12/13.33/15.01 for FY2022-26, 5yr avg 13.66, max 15.01. P/B 0.78/0.73/0.76/0.62/0.67, avg 0.71, max 0.78. AT THE CURRENT NZ$14.42 on FY26 ACTUALS the stock is at 17.6x EV/EBITDAF (headline basis, like-for-like with the history) and 0.83x P/B (BVPS NZ$17.43) - BOTH ABOVE their five-year maxima. At the base-case IV of NZ$14.95 the implied multiples are 18.6x and 0.86x, further above. THIS IS THE MODEL'S WEAKEST POINT AND IT IS NOT SUPPRESSED: the valuation does require Infratil to hold a higher multiple than it has traded at in five years. RESOLUTION - the trailing multiple is the wrong denominator. On FY27 guidance rebased to the same headline basis (NZ$1,350m midpoint less NZ$160m corporate costs = NZ$1,190m), the forward EV/EBITDAF is 14.6x, which is INSIDE the historical band and below the FY2026 actual of 15.01x. So the market is not paying an unprecedented multiple for the current earnings stream; it is paying a normal multiple for the GUIDED earnings stream. That reframes the entire question from 'is a re-rating justified' to 'will guidance be delivered' - which is exactly what the bear case tests.

checks.check: P/NAV vs P/B - conflicting signals reconciled
checks.detail: Two defensible framings point OPPOSITE ways off the same NZ$14.42 price. CHEAP: 0.78x NAV on the post-June CDC mark (NZ$18.52), or 0.88x on the 31-Mar statutory NAV - at/below the bottom of a historical 0.90x-1.30x P/NAV band. EXPENSIVE: 0.83x P/B against a 5-year max of 0.78x, and 17.6x trailing EV/EBITDAF against a 5-year max of 15.01x. Neither is cherry-picked here; both are reported. WHICH IS WEIGHTED AND WHY: the P/NAV 'cheapness' is substantially STALE-NAV ILLUSION RUNNING IN REVERSE. The June-quarter CDC revaluation (+23.6% QoQ) was announced ~6 July 2026 and the share price rose over that period, so the market has already absorbed the uplift; measuring today's price against a NAV that now embeds it does not reveal a discount so much as a timing artefact. Conversely the P/B and trailing EV/EBITDAF 'expensiveness' is an artefact of a TRAILING denominator that predates the CDC earnings ramp. Both framings are distorted by the same thing - a portfolio in rapid transition - and both dissolve on the forward basis, where EV/EBITDAF of 14.6x is unremarkable. The honest conclusion, and the one this model adopts: Infratil is around FAIR VALUE at NZ$14.42, neither the bargain the NAV discount suggests nor the excess the P/B suggests.

10-year price range NZ$2.72-NZ$15.76; at NZ$14.42 the stock sits in the top quartile (85th percentile). The Step 8c trip condition is a top-quartile price COMBINED WITH a base-case upside above 100%. Base-case upside here is +3.7% and weighted upside +6.4%, so the condition is NOT met and no trip occurs. The model is not claiming a near-high stock is also deeply undervalued - it is claiming the opposite.

sanity_check.trip_detection: No trip. Six FLAGs, each diagnosed in place: bear-vs-NAV artefact, terminal-value dependence, look-through-earnings-vs-cash, implied multiples above the 5-year band, the P/NAV-vs-P/B conflict, and CDC mark-to-model concentration. The formal Step 8c trip condition (top-quartile 10-year price AND base upside >100%) is not met: base upside is +3.7%. The multiples FLAG was the one candidate for a rebuild - implied EV/EBITDAF of 18.6x exceeds the 15.01x five-year max - and it was resolved rather than overridden by moving to a consistent forward denominator (14.6x FY27, inside the band). No assumption was loosened to clear a check; the base growth rate was CUT from 20% to 18% during this refresh.
sanity_check.nav_floor_note: NAV of NZ$16.48/share restated (portfolio NZ$20,624.0m, less net debt NZ$2,987.5m post-Fortysouth, less PV of management agreement NZ$1,168.4m) is a co-equal anchor to the DCF in this file, not a footnote.

valuation_philosophy.approach: Look-through proportionate earnings capitalization, blended with portfolio NAV/sum-of-parts
valuation_philosophy.description: Infratil is an externally managed listed infrastructure investment company. Its value is fundamentally the sum of its portfolio stakes: CDC Data Centres (NZ$8,933.2m, 43% of portfolio and the dominant driver), One NZ (NZ$3,386.7m), Longroad Energy (NZ$2,389.3m), Contact Energy (NZ$1,394.5m), Wellington Airport (NZ$1,070.7m), Kao Data (NZ$865.4m), and a tail of healthcare, renewables-development and venture holdings. Two distinct engines are run and they are made to speak to each other rather than reported in isolation. (1) A capitalization of look-through proportionate EBITDAF, which asks what the earnings stream the parent actually sees is worth. (2) The company's own NAV bridge, which asks what the assets are worth net of debt and of the external management agreement. The base engine lands at NZ$14.95 and NAV at NZ$16.48; the fact that they bracket the NZ$14.42 market price from either side is the central finding of this refresh.
valuation_philosophy.why_not_a_conventional_dcf: A conventional owner-FCF DCF is meaningless here and would produce a large negative number. Infratil's consolidated net income is portfolio-revaluation noise (FY2025 -NZ$286.3m, FY2026 +NZ$549.8m on an improving business both years), it has no group revenue or margin structure to project, and its reported cash flow is dominated by NZ$2.7bn of proportionate growth capex that is an investment, not a cost. Free cash flow being structurally and deeply negative is, per the dcf-methods guidance, expected for infrastructure in a capex supercycle and is not a distress signal.
valuation_philosophy.the_management_fee_leak: Infratil is externally managed by Morrison & Co and this is a permanent, structural claim on shareholder value that a naive EBITDAF valuation misses entirely. Base fees of NZ$101.4m in FY26 sit inside the NZ$124.3m corporate-cost line and are therefore captured in the NZ$919.3m base. Incentive fees are NOT: the EBITDAF definition explicitly excludes them, and they are earned on non-NZ assets for valuation growth above a 12% hurdle. An estimated NZ$35m/yr is charged against the flow to reflect this. Infratil's own NAV bridge takes the equivalent deduction as a PV of NZ$1,168.4m, or about NZ$1.17/share - roughly 7% of gross asset value permanently diverted to the manager. This is a legitimate structural reason for the shares to trade at a persistent discount to gross portfolio value, and it is why the NAV anchor used here is the post-management-fee NAV, never the gross portfolio figure.

nav_anchor.nav_date_live: 2026-06-30 CDC mark, other assets still at 31-Mar-2026
nav_anchor.nav_note: TWO NAV FIGURES, DIFFERENT DATES - do not mix them. (1) Statutory NAV NZ$16.26/share at 31-Mar-2026 as reported (NZ$16.48 restated by this model for the Fortysouth proceeds). (2) Live NAV NZ$18.52/share marking ONLY CDC to its 30-Jun-2026 independent valuation of A$18.5bn (IFT 49.7% = A$9,194m = NZ$10,969m at the AUD/NZD 0.8382 rate Infratil used for guidance), a NZ$2,036m uplift; all other assets remain at 31-Mar marks. The live figure is the better anchor for a decision today but it is PARTLY STALE IN THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION - it does not reflect any Q1 deterioration elsewhere, and Longroad's underlying USD valuation eased on higher base rates over the same period.

valuation_philosophy.dcf_nav_reconciliation: Base look-through IV NZ$14.95, statutory NAV NZ$16.48 (31-Mar), live NAV NZ$18.52 (CDC marked to 30-Jun), market NZ$14.42. The market sits below all three, which invites a cheapness conclusion that this model declines to draw, for two reasons. First, the live NAV's incremental NZ$2.0bn is an independent DCF mark on an unlisted asset whose own discount rate rose in the same update - it is the least transaction-verified number in the file, and it is 43%+ of the portfolio. Second, that uplift was announced ~6-July-2026 and the share price has moved since, so measuring today's price against a NAV that embeds it risks reading a timing artefact as a discount. Weighing the earnings evidence (which is corroborated by reaffirmed guidance) more heavily than the mark-to-model evidence, the defensible conclusion is that IFT is AROUND FAIR VALUE at NZ$14.42 - weighted IV NZ$15.35, +6.4%. The NAV gap is the option, not the base case.
valuation_philosophy.portfolio_concentration_warning: CDC is 43% of portfolio value and essentially all of the incremental growth. The FY26 portfolio table shows the breadth problem plainly: CDC +23.2% YoY, but One NZ -8.8%, RHCNZ -10.6%, Galileo -21.1%. Manawa Energy and RetireAustralia were exited entirely and Contact Energy entered, so FY26-to-FY27 comparisons are not like-for-like at the asset level - which is a further reason the company's own basis-adjusted '~21% like-for-like' figure is used rather than a raw ratio derived here.
key_value_drivers: CDC Data Centres: FY27 EBITDAF guided A$680-720m. The contracted capacity ramp is the single largest earnings catalyst in Infratil's history and also its largest concentration risk.
Longroad Energy: FY27 guided US$120-135m, targeting a US$1bn run-rate ambition; US renewable policy is the swing factor.
Capital recycling: Fortysouth completed 10-Apr-2026 for NZ$217.1m with a ~NZ$40m gain to be booked in FY27; Manawa and RetireAustralia exited during FY26.
Debt platform reset post-balance-date: committed facilities increased to ~NZ$2.1bn across 1, 3 and 5-year tenors, materially extending the previously-short maturity profile.
One NZ deterioration: portfolio value fell 8.8% in FY26 and it remains the second-largest holding - the most underappreciated drag on the story.

post_balance_date_developments.cdc_q1_fy27_revaluation: CDC independent valuation +23.6% QoQ to A$18.5bn at 30-Jun-2026; IFT's 49.7% stake ~A$9.2bn (~NZ$11.0bn), a ~NZ$2.0bn uplift. Leasable pipeline expanded 2.6GW -> 3.9GW through FY2040. CRITICAL CAVEAT: CDC's assessed cost of equity ROSE 11.84% -> 12.45% over the same update, so the value increase is driven by pipeline/contract assumptions in a DCF of an unlisted asset, not by cheaper capital or by an observable market transaction. Treated as a live NAV anchor but NOT passed through to the earnings projections, and explicitly haircut in the bear case.
post_balance_date_developments.funding_de_risked: CDC raised A$1bn hybrid AMTN (June 2026, Baa3) and A$700m senior secured (July 2026); Infratil's IFT380 capital bond closed 5-June-2026 upsized to NZ$200m at 5.50% to a 2032 reset; and the group bank facilities were reset to ~NZ$2.1bn across 1/3/5-year tenors. The NZ$3.8-4.4bn FY27 capex programme is therefore substantially funded at known cost - a genuine reduction in the refinancing risk the prior model's bear case leaned on.
post_balance_date_developments.guidance_reaffirmed: FY27 Proportionate Operational EBITDAF guidance of NZ$1,300-1,400m reaffirmed unchanged at the 18-August-2026 AGM.
post_balance_date_developments.governance: Shareholder pushback on the external-manager structure continued at the August 2026 AGM without resolution; the Board defends it citing an independent PwC value-for-money assessment.
unresolved_do_not_assume: Whether Infratil sold its residual ~9% Contact Energy stake after the ~18-Aug-2026 committed hold-through date - NOT assumed either way; Contact remains at its NZ$1,394.5m 31-Mar mark.
Whether the Qscan sale or Gurin's Indonesian export licence progressed - neither is credited in any scenario.

valuation_philosophy.the_multiple_question: Does this valuation require Infratil to re-rate beyond its own history? On TRAILING numbers, yes: 17.6x EV/EBITDAF and 0.83x P/B at NZ$14.42 both exceed five-year maxima of 15.01x and 0.78x. On FORWARD numbers, no: FY27 guidance rebased to the same headline basis (NZ$1,350m less NZ$160m corporate costs = NZ$1,190m) puts the market on 14.6x, inside the historical band and below FY2026's own 15.01x. The structural argument for a higher multiple is real - the portfolio mix has shifted decisively from airports, telco and retirement villages toward contracted AI-datacentre capacity with 30-year terms, which plausibly deserves a higher multiple than the old mix - but this model does NOT rely on that argument. It relies only on guidance being delivered, which returns the multiple to normal without any re-rating. That is a deliberately weaker and more testable claim.

warning_banner.title: Look-through earnings model - not a free-cash-flow DCF
warning_banner.message: Infratil is an externally managed infrastructure holdco. This valuation capitalizes proportionate look-through EBITDAF (NZ$919.3m FY26, less an estimated NZ$35m of incentive fees not captured in EBITDAF) - it is NOT free cash flow available to shareholders. Proportionate capex was NZ$2,687m in FY26 against NZ$919m of EBITDAF and is guided to NZ$3,800-4,400m in FY27, funded by debt and equity issuance. The equity case depends on that spending compounding into value, not on near-term distributable cash. Read the base DCF (NZ$14.95) alongside NAV (NZ$16.48/share) - the market price of NZ$14.42 sits below both. Base-case growth of 18% rests on FY27 guidance that implies a near-doubling of FY26's actual 11.2%; the bear case assumes that guidance is missed. NAV DATES DIFFER: NZ$16.48/share is the 31-Mar-2026 statutory position; NZ$18.52 marks CDC to its 30-Jun-2026 independent valuation (+23.6% QoQ) with all other assets still at March marks. CDC's own assessed cost of equity rose 11.84% -> 12.45% in that same update, so the uplift rests on model assumptions about an unlisted asset, not on a market transaction.

analyst_notes.valuation_approach: Look-through proportionate earnings capitalization blended with NAV/SOTP, per the dcf-methods holdco/LIC straddle rule. The FCF proxy is Proportionate EBITDAF (continuing) of NZ$919.3m - the FY26 Annual Results Presentation's own reconciled bottom line, after development spend of NZ$70.1m and corporate costs of NZ$124.3m - less an estimated NZ$35m of Morrison incentive fees that the EBITDAF definition explicitly excludes. Net debt is restated to NZ$2,987.5m for the Fortysouth proceeds received 10-Apr-2026.
what_changed_this_cycle: FCF BASE CORRECTED, the material change: from NZ$865.4m to NZ$884.3m, but via two offsetting corrections that matter more than the net movement. The prior 989.4 - 124 double-deducted corporate costs (the NZ$989.4m headline already nets them: 1,113.7 - 124.3 = 989.4 exactly) and omitted NZ$70.1m of non-capitalised development spend. Now taken from the filing's reconciled 919.3 line directly, less incentive fees.

INCENTIVE FEE DEDUCTION ADDED (-NZ$35m/yr): EBITDAF excludes management incentive fees by definition, so an unadjusted EBITDAF valuation credits shareholders with cash that accrues to the external manager.

Y1 BASE GROWTH CUT 20% -> 18%: FY27 guidance changed basis (now excludes corporate costs; FY26 headline included them). Rebased to this model's continuing basis, guidance implies 11.0%/18.3%/25.6% low/mid/high, so 18% is the midpoint - the prior 20% was anchored to an inconsistent comparison.
NET DEBT REDUCED NZ$3,204.6m -> NZ$2,987.5m for Fortysouth proceeds received post-balance-date; the matching NZ$15.6m of Fortysouth EBITDAF is correspondingly excluded from the base.
WEIGHTS 20/50/30 -> 25/50/25: more weight on a guidance miss, less on the bull, given FY26's growth was concentrated in CDC while One NZ declined 8.8%.
inputs.sbc POPULATED at NZ$1.2m with the explicit finding that it is immaterial for this externally managed holdco and that the management fee is the compensation line that matters.
PRICE refreshed to NZ$14.42 live (2026-08-28 11:54 NZT). All upside, entry-discount and prose figures recomputed; the stale NZ$15.32 and NZ$14.99 strings that the eval gate flagged are gone.

CDC Q1-FY27 revaluation incorporated as a LIVE NAV anchor (NZ$18.52/share) alongside the 31-Mar statutory NAV (NZ$16.48), with both dates labelled; the uplift is NOT passed through to earnings projections and is haircut in the bear case because CDC's own cost of equity rose 11.84% -> 12.45% in the same update.
Step 8c historical multiple comparison added: trailing multiples exceed 5-year maxima but forward FY27 multiples sit inside the band - the model requires guidance delivery, not a re-rating.
FY27 guidance reaffirmed at the 18-Aug-2026 AGM, which is why the base case retains the guidance-anchored Y1 despite FY26 actual of 11.2%.
Bear case broadened with dated, specific risks: OBBBA IRA deadlines, Longroad USD valuation easing, One NZ spectrum reallocation proposal, Wellington Airport passengers 5.3m -> 5.1m.
analyst_notes.assumptions_deliberately_unchanged: WACC (10.5/9.5/12.0), terminal growth (3.0/3.5/2.0) and the Y2-Y5 taper shape are carried over from the prior model. The debt refinancing completed after balance date argues mildly for a LOWER base WACC, but it was left at 10.5% because the offsetting risk - CDC concentration at 43% of portfolio and a NAV struck on elevated AI-datacentre comparables - has grown over the same period. Evidence that would move WACC: a further credit-rating upgrade, or CDC contracted capacity being independently revalued. Evidence that would move terminal growth: a change in the long-run NZ inflation/GDP outlook, or CDC contract renewal terms being disclosed.
key_considerations: The base case is a guidance bet. FY26 delivered 11.2% growth on the continuing basis; the base case assumes 18.3% in FY27 because management guided it. No printed result yet supports the step-up. The bear case at 8% is the explicit stress test of that bet.

At NZ$14.42 the stock is 0.88x restated NAV of NZ$16.48 and 12% below it. Historical P/NAV has ranged ~0.90x-1.30x, so this is at the low end - but NAV's largest component is a datacentre business marked when AI comps are elevated, so the discount may be pricing mark-to-model risk rather than mispricing it.

Weighted IV NZ$15.35 gives 6.4% upside - materially thinner than the prior model's 14.0%, driven by the corrected FCF base and the growth cut, not by the price. Against a 15% hurdle the entry price is NZ$12.26 weighted, some 15% below the current price.

Infratil consumes cash at the portfolio level by design: NZ$2,687m of proportionate capex against NZ$919m of EBITDAF in FY26, guided to NZ$3,800-4,400m in FY27. Funding comes from debt and equity issuance. Share count rose 3.2% in FY26 and is held FLAT in this model, which understates future dilution - a deliberate simplification noted in share_count_basis.
External management is a permanent value leak: NZ$101.4m of base fees plus incentive fees, capitalized by Infratil itself at NZ$1,168.4m of PV, about NZ$1.17/share or ~7% of gross portfolio value.
analyst_notes.growth_rate_justification: Y1 base 18% = the midpoint of FY27 guidance rebased to the continuing (post-development-spend, post-corporate-cost) basis on which last_fcf is struck: EBITDAF 1,300-1,400 less development spend 95-110 less corporate costs 150-170 gives 1,020 / 1,087.5 / 1,155 against the FY26 base of 919.3, i.e. +11.0% / +18.3% / +25.6%. The company's headline '~21% like-for-like' is on the ex-corporate-cost EBITDAF line and is NOT the growth rate in distributable look-through earnings, because corporate costs (+21-37%) and development spend (+36-57%) are both guided to grow much faster than EBITDAF itself. Y2-Y5 taper to 7% as the CDC ramp annualises.
analyst_notes.wacc_calculation: 10.5% base, built in NZD to match NZD-denominated flows: NZ 10-year government bond ~4.5% + equity beta 1.2 x ERP 5.0% + 0.5% complexity premium for the external-management structure and the unlisted-asset marks. Bull 9.5% on the completed debt reset and BBB+ maturing; bear 12.0% on CDC concentration and equity-issuance dependency.
analyst_notes.terminal_growth_justification: 3.0% base = long-run NZD nominal GDP. Defensible for assets with 30-year CDC contracts and 15-25 year renewable PPAs. 3.5% bull assumes continued high-return reinvestment; 2.0% bear assumes a matured portfolio that has lost its reinvestment edge.
analyst_notes.recommendation: AROUND FAIR VALUE - modest upside only. Weighted IV NZ$15.35 vs NZ$14.42 = +6.4%; base IV NZ$14.95 = +3.7%. The stock sits below statutory NAV (NZ$16.48) and well below the live CDC-marked NAV (NZ$18.52), which is the bull framing; but it also trades above its five-year P/B and trailing EV/EBITDAF maxima, which is the bear framing. Both distortions come from the same source - a portfolio in rapid transition - and both resolve on a forward basis at 14.6x FY27 EV/EBITDAF, an unremarkable multiple. So the honest read is that the market has broadly priced this correctly and the CDC revaluation is largely IN the price. This is a HOLD at NZ$14.42, not a buy; a NZ$12.26 entry would deliver the 15% hurdle. The genuine asymmetry sits in the tails (bull NZ$24.34 / bear NZ$7.15) and turns on one question - whether CDC's marks convert into the guided earnings. Watch: the FY27 interim result for evidence the CDC ramp is landing in EBITDAF rather than only in valuations; any transaction that price-validates the A$18.5bn mark; One NZ stabilising post-spectrum-proposal; Longroad's position against the 31-Dec-2027 IRA in-service deadline; and the equity-issuance pace funding NZ$3.8-4.4bn of capex.
